Neural Engine research update: NumPy/SciPy linear algebra and SHA-256 compatibility.

We investigated free, open-source numerical implementations for the linear operations inside our recurrent Neural Engine. NumPy supports the matrix products; SciPy provides direct solves and reusable LU/QR factorizations. SymPy is a complementary symbolic option, but was not installed or tested in this investigation.

For equilibrium susceptibility, chi = (I - D K)^(-1) D W can be computed by solving (I - D K) chi = D W. The five saved-state susceptibility cases agreed with the recorded values within the existing tolerances. This checks the linear calculation at saved fields; it is not new equilibrium or gradient validation.

Original synthetic CPU timings, inverse-plus-product versus general solve including factorization:
- 12 neurons: 0.032387 ms versus 0.077600 ms.
- 142 neurons: 1.214487 ms versus 0.587696 ms.
- 600 neurons: 35.296283 ms versus 11.786771 ms.

The 600-neuron operation was about 3x faster with the direct solve; the 12-neuron case was slower. Both results are preserved. Conditions: float64, four right-hand sides, one OpenBLAS thread, seven timing blocks; imports, matrix construction, serialization, and whole-engine execution excluded. These are operation timings, not measured whole-engine speedups.

SHA-256 identifiers remain compatible with these libraries. A 256-bit digest does not require 256-bit neural arithmetic. Cross-language canonical serialization, numerical tolerance checks, and SHA-derived random-stream definitions must be preserved. Numerically equivalent results can have different hashes when their last floating-point bits differ.

This publication records research findings and a reproducible numerical check. It does not change production equations, the sigmoid, training rules, or random streams. Full-gradient optimization and end-to-end performance validation remain future work.
